newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: UNIDO chief to step down over donor apathy.
newsitem.headline: UNIDO chief to step down over donor apathy.

text.p: The head of the U.N.'s industrial development organisation (UNIDO) said on Monday he would not seek re-election at the end of the year because of a lack of commitment to the body by major Western nations.

Mauricio de Maria y Campos, UNIDO director-general since April 1993, said that despite major reforms to the organisation, which have included a big reduction in staff, there was still insufficient support from some member nations.

"It is this continued lack of commitment on the side of some key donor countries and the resulting uncertainty which have led me to take my decision," Maria y Campos of Mexico told a special session of the Vienna-based body's industrial development board.

The United States, widely criticised for failing to honour in full its budgetary commitments to the United Nations, pulled out of UNIDO last December. Maria y Campos said Washington had still not paid its outstanding contributions. Britain also plans to withdraw by the end of 1997 and Germany last year considered doing the same but backed down.

UNIDO promotes industrialisation in the developing world and has also helped former European communist states. It has reformed its strategy by helping also to promote free market economies but some governments have lost interest in the body in order to cut costs.
